title: Which catalog row explains a T6 Zombies crash, what kind of thing caused it, which script owns it, and which line says so

fields.crash_text: The crash .txt written beside the minidump: exception code, last com error message, last gsc error message, last gsc pos
fields.console_before_crash: Up to 40 console lines before the crash from console_zm.log, engine timestamps kept, dvar dump lines dropped

signature.instructions: This is a Plutonium T6 Zombies crash: the crash text the engine wrote, and the console lines just before it. Which catalog row names the cause of this crash? Pick the row whose cause the crash text or console lines actually show. The 'position only' row applies only when the last gsc pos names a script path with '::' after it, such as maps/mp/_x::fn, and there is no error message; a bare '::function' with no path before it is not a script position and that row does not apply. If a com error message in words names something no row lists, pick none.

plus.none: No catalog row names the cause shown in this crash text or console

culprit_kind.instructions: What kind of thing most likely caused this crash, judging only from the crash text and the console lines?

criteria.script_logic: A GSC script read an undefined value, cast it wrongly, or called a function with a bad argument; the crash text names a gsc error message
criteria.hard_limit: The engine hit a fixed capacity: no free entities, configstring overflow, asset count, client field space, memory; the com error or console names the limit
criteria.asset_missing: A referenced asset, animation, sound bank, image or file was absent or failed to parse; the console names what was missing
criteria.position_only: The crash text names a script position but no error message and no com error, and the console shows no failure line; the cause is not shown
criteria.engine_internal: An engine fault with no script position and no mod-attributable message

owner_script.instructions: Which script named anywhere in the crash text or console is the most likely owner of the defect? The 'last gsc pos' names where the VM was when it died, which is usually but not always the owner; a com error naming a spawn or limit points at the script that was spawning.

plus.none_named: No script is named, or none of the named scripts is clearly the owner

evidence_line.instructions: Which single line of the crash text most directly justifies the signature you would pick?

plus.none: No single line of the crash text justifies a signature; the console lines carry the evidence, or nothing does

has_message_in_words.instructions: Does the crash text carry an engine error message in words, in the 'last com error message' or 'last gsc error message' field, rather than only an exception code and a position?

criteria.true: At least one of the two message fields is non-empty and states a cause in words, such as 'cannot cast undefined to bool' or 'G_Spawn: no free entities'
criteria.false: Both message fields are empty quotes; only the exception code and the gsc pos remain

policy.note: Regex runs first and is authoritative when it matches a specific row. This set is consulted when regex matches nothing or only the generic position row. Above act: the answer may be shown as the likely row. A catalog gap is derived in code: has_message_in_words true and signature none. Never promotes a signature; a derived gap queues the crash for a person.
